subtitle: Lesson 20 · Core ITIL 4 Practices: Request, Knowledge & Service Level

code:
Purpose: maintain and improve the effective,
efficient use of information and knowledge
across the organization.

The emphasis is on USE -- not on how much
documentation exists.
caption: Mountains of documents still fail if nobody can find the right one.

steps.label: Data
steps.sub: unprocessed facts -- 400 failed logins at 2 a.m.

steps.label: Information
steps.sub: data with context -- all from one IP, outside hours

steps.label: Knowledge
steps.sub: information plus experience -- this looks like credential stuffing

steps.label: Wisdom
steps.sub: applying that knowledge with judgment to this situation, right now

code:
The trap: a separate documentation project --
a backlog that grows while nobody reads it.

The better pattern: capture knowledge as a
byproduct of work already happening.

Resolve a major incident -> write it up right
after, while details are fresh.
caption: The write-up costs little extra right after the fix.

code:
Most orgs already have a wiki or knowledge base.
Storage is rarely the gap.

The gap is behavior:
- Will the resolver take 2 extra minutes to write it up?
- Will the next person search before calling?
caption: Knowledge management succeeds or fails on those two habits.

subtitle: Setting clear targets for how good a service has to be.
